quotes: Our total income should exceed last year's figures, in spite of rates having gone down by as much as it has, especially in Singapore. We expect rates to remain at current levels... SORA, we expect SORA to stay around the 1.2 or so for the average of the rest of the year.
We raised our commercial book non-interest income growth to mid-teens because wealth management is really firing on all cylinders, and we hope to continue.
We want to keep our cost-to-income ratio in the low 40s. So far, we've been around 39, 40. We want to keep that discipline. Assume SP within the range that we have guided of 17 to 20 basis points.

result.evidence: Growth up (Hong Kong +23%) while 'Net interest margin' is guided/reported DOWN (driver: Interest rates were broadly stable; more than offset by balance sheet growth). Margin compression — value on margin trajectory, not top-line growth.
result.outcome_note: [reading] Net interest margin is guided/reported down despite Hong Kong revenue growth of +23%. | anomalous: Revenue growth and margin compression are diverging; the driver is balance sheet expansion outpacing interest income accretion under stable interest rates, indicating volume-driven growth is diluting per-unit yield. | affects: margin, growth rate, segment multiple | conf 95% | VERDICT: NIM compression driven by balance sheet growth rather than rate declines means valuation sensitivity shifts from volume expansion to yield preservation.

points: We expect non-interest income to remain the primary growth driver, with bancassurance providing counter-cyclical diversification to investment-linked WM fees, while improving HK CRE conditions offer optionality on GP writebacks.

We continue to prefer DBS among the Singapore banks given its capital return plans (until FY27), fixed DPS policy, and high dividend payout ratio (dividend yield FY26e: 5.6%, FY27e: 6.1%), which offer greater stability compared to its peers, which follow a floating payout ratio tied to earnings perf
Institutional equities are emerging as a quiet new growth lever (cash equities +77% YoY, total IE +36%).
catalysts: Improving HK CRE conditions and faster-than-expected repayment of HK real estate loans.
Potential for GP writebacks on HK exposures if conditions continue to improve.
Intact capital return architecture (S$5bn dividends + S$3bn buyback, total S$8bn) until FY27.
Strong wealth management momentum (record WM fees, AUM reached S$492bn, net new money of S$10bn).
risks: NIM compression continues; rate sensitivity rising. NII sensitivity has risen to S$11mn per bp for SGD due to higher CASA mix. Every additional 25 bps SORA cut translates into a ~S$275mn NII headwind.
Management declined to commit to the implied 6 cents quarterly DPS step-up at end-FY26, citing Iran-related uncertainty.
A prolonged Iran conflict may lower loan growth by a couple of billion.

revisions.reason: Nudging up FY26e earnings by 1% from higher wealth management estimates

result.description: DBS Group Holdings Ltd provides commercial banking and financial services in Singapore, Hong Kong, rest of Greater China, South and Southeast Asia, and internationally. It operates through Personal Banking; Institutional Banking; and Global Financial Markets segments. The Personal Banking segment offers banking and related financial services, including current and savings accounts, fixed deposits, loans and home finance, cards, payments, investment, and insurance products for individual customers. The Institutional Banking segment provides financial services and products comprise short-term working capital financing and specialized lending; cash management, trade finance, and securities and fiduciary services; treasury and markets products; corporate finance and advisory banking services; and capital markets solutions for bank and non-bank financial institutions, government-linked companies, large corporates, and small and medium sized businesses. The Global Financial Markets segment is involved in the structuring, market-making, and trading in various treasury products. DBS Group Holdings Ltd was founded in 1968 and is headquartered in Singapore.
